In `watch-pr/`, when both check sources are empty, `resolveChecks` asks GitHub whether the repository runs checks (`runsChecks`, `PR_RUNS_CHECKS_QUERY`: a `.yml` or `.yaml` file in `.github/workflows` on the PR head or the base branch whose `on` names a `pull_request*` event, or a `push` unless its `branches` lists only the base branch or it has only `tags` or `tags-ignore` filters, or whose triggers `Bun.YAML` cannot read, a check on an earlier commit of the PR, a check on one of the repository's 10 most recently updated pull requests, or a protection rule or ruleset that requires checks). With none, the read is `source: "no-ci"` with zero checks, and the status table shows `✅ no CI`.
In `watch-pr/policy.ts`, `runSimple` runs a `--status-only` read with `maxQueryErrors: 1`, so a query error returns the `status-query` blocker at once instead of retrying.

In `watch-pr/`, add `--once` (`PollingOptions.once`): `deadlinePassed` returns true when `once`, so the watcher makes one classifying read, never sleeps and prints no `WAITING` or `RETRY` line. `READY` and `BLOCKER` come as usual; a pending PR ends at `TIMEOUT` with reason `pending-checks`, which names its `frontier`, or `queued-stack` with `--queued-stack`, exit 5; a retryable query error, stack discovery included, ends at `TIMEOUT` with reason `status-unavailable` (`statusUnavailableVerdict`) even under `--max-query-errors 1`, and a non-retryable one at the `status-query` blocker. The `status-unavailable` reason's `pr` names the PR whose read failed (`readingPr`), or is null when the PR context itself could not be read. `runJson` reads a `gh` error that says `Could not resolve to a PullRequest` or `Repository`, or `no pull requests found`, as the non-retryable `not-found`, so a missing PR or a branch with no PR ends at the `status-query` blocker. The `queued-stack` timeout carries `waitingOn` (`FrontierWait`): `pending-checks`, `review-required` with `requestedReviewers`, or `merge`. `parsePullRequest` reads gh's `reviewRequests` into `requestedReviewers` (the first non-empty of a user's `login`, a team's `slug` or its `name`), and the READY gate carries them. `--pretty` READY with `REVIEW_REQUIRED` and none requested prints `note=review required, none requested`. `--once` conflicts with `--status-only`.
